label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa contra gentiles I.16: Act is SIMPLY_PRIOR_1 to POTENCY_1: whatever is in…
locator: I.16 [3]: absolutely speaking act is prior to potency
interpretation: Though a thing that is first in potency and then in act is in time in potency first, act is absolutely prior, because potency does not raise itself to act but must be raised by something in act; hence 'whatever is in some way in potency has something prior to it'. Read as the same simple priority of act as ST I q.3 a.1 co. (claim AQUINAS-ST-I-Q3-A1-ACT-SIMPLY-PRIOR-A): the potency in question is reduced by a being in act, so the prior being is in act in the respect in which the other is in potency. The SCG wording does not state the respect explicitly; that detail rests on 'raised to act by something that is in act'. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
